items.rootCause: I traced, from the code and the APK 18/19 measurements, what still sits between GO! and the board. The game's state reaches the phone X = 17–189 ms after GO! is drawn, because the server only starts the game at GO. app/friends/room.tsx opened the game screen only once room.phase became 'game', so all of this ran after the state arrived and before the game screen's own mount could start: the push, the navigator commit of the new screen, GameRoute, GoCover's 'cover' commit (FriendsGoFrame: the header, the subtitle and 2–4 SVG avatars of about 120 RNSVG paths each, mounted on the UI thread), GoCover's afterFrames(1), and removing the room screen (dropWhenCovered). That whole chain sat on the critical path every time, while the wait for the game (X) sat in front of it doing nothing. The rest of the path is unchanged and still the largest part: the GameScreen mount itself (about 0.5–0.85 s from mount start to StatusBarModule on APK 18), then SWAP_FRAMES and the 150 ms fade. Sounds were already handled in loop 12. Fonts and Skia are not in the first commit (the warp canvas and the hit banner stand by from 2–2.25 s after the board).
items.fix:
1) app/friends/room.tsx: the game screen now opens as soon as GO! shows, or when the game arrives if that comes first. It is no longer held back until the game arrives. A rejoin into a running game still gets a plain push.
2) GoCover.tsx gets a new `waiting` prop and gameOnItsWay / useGameOnItsWay. For a friends GO! whose game has not arrived yet (no hasGame and the room not closed), GoCover keeps GO! up and mounts nothing under it. The friends room's online lobby never shows under GO!. When the game arrives, the game is mounted under GO! in that same render, with no extra frame: the cover was drawn long before. A new coverDrawn state replaces afterFrames(1) → setPhase('under'), so a GO! with no wait behaves exactly as before. The ranked GO! is untouched, because gameOnItsWay returns false for it.
3) app/game.tsx: passes waiting = useGameOnItsWay(goCover, online?.connection) to GoCover.
The result: the push, the route, the cover's first draw (with its avatars), afterFrames(1) and dropping the room all now happen while the game is still on its way.
4) room.tsx guard: on the first count render the tick's last value (useNow) is stale. It was read in the lobby, or on the phone's own clock before the session existed. In tests, and on a phone with a wrong clock, that showed GO! for one render. Before this change that was harmless; now it would open the game screen early. So while counting, the count now reads the session clock fresh on every render. The 100 ms tick stops once GO! is shown, so the room does nothing under the game.
The loop 15 slam and handoff (useSlamSince, FriendsGoFrame, goFadeFrom/goFadeOf) are unchanged. Hit banner standby (HIT_BANNER_STANDBY_DELAY_MS) and the other warm-ups still start from the GameScreen mount, which still comes only after the game arrives, so they all stay after the board. No new strings and no new animation. Comments updated in goHandoff.ts, and the friends.countdown row in docs/design/motion.md is updated.
items.test:

1) src/screens/friends/__tests__/friendsRoutes.test.tsx, 'GO! by my clock, the game not here yet…'. On the real room route, GO! by the phone clock with no game from the server must already be at /game: friends-go-frame with GO!, 'מכינים את הלוח…', and a FriendsGo handed over. For 150 ms of server time nothing is mounted under GO!. After startGame the game appears under GO!. Old room.tsx: Expected '/game', Received '/friends/room'. The StubGame in this file now mirrors app/game.tsx (useGameOnItsWay).
2) src/screens/match/__tests__/GoCover.test.tsx, 'handed over as GO! shows, the game still on its way…', with Reduced Motion off and on. 10 frames with waiting: GO! alone, no mount, back does nothing. Then waiting=false: the game is mounted at UNDER_OPACITY in that very render (no frame waited), and fades in as before, mounted once. Plus a pure test of gameOnItsWay: friends GO! and lobby/reconnecting give true; hasGame, closed, a ranked GO!, null model or null info give false. Old GoCover: 3 failed (the game mounted while waiting; gameOnItsWay missing).
3) The stale-count guard is covered by the existing friendsRoutes tests: without the fresh clock read, 16 of them failed because the room jumped to GO! and /game when the count started.

rep.notes:
1) Why partial: this change takes off the critical path what comes before the game screen's mount: the push, the route, the GO! cover with its avatars, afterFrames(1) and dropping the room. The saving is limited by X, the time from GO! to the game's state (17–189 ms), so it is at most about 0.05–0.2 s. The mount itself is still on the path (about 0.5–0.85 s on the phones), so ≤1.0 s is not guaranteed. The only remaining lever to bring GO!→board under 1.0 s is to mount the game during 3·2·1. That needs the server to send the game (givens) at the countdown with startsAt, plus a client view of a game that has not started yet. It is a protocol and GameRoom change with compatibility work and a deploy, so I did not make it in the last round.
2) Behaviour change in a rare case: if the room closes in the gap between GO! and the game's arrival (about 0.1–0.2 s), the game route's connection error with its exits is shown instead of the room's 'closed' state. The room is already out of the history by then. If the connection drops during that gap, GO! stays on screen with 'מכינים את הלוח…' until the game arrives or the room closes, as the room screen did before.
3) A latent bug found and fixed along the way: on the first count render, the room computed the step from a stale useNow value (taken in the lobby, or from the phone's clock before the session existed), which could show GO! for one render. That was harmless before; with the push at GO! it would have opened the game screen at the start of the count. The count now reads the session clock fresh on every render.
4) prettier --write on docs/design/motion.md reformatted the whole file (tables and JSON). I rebuilt it from HEAD plus my 2 sentence edits only. Before doing that I confirmed that the prettier-formatted HEAD differs from the file only in my edits, so no other agent's change was lost. The diff is now 1 line. All files are LF.
5) To check that the tests fail on the old code, I swapped in room.tsx and GoCover.tsx from snap-loop16 for a moment and restored them right away (hashes checked). Backups are in C:/Users/mosheg/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/b0377245321c840d/6deeb02e-1cd6-480d-8ffd-14ec3cc5da59/scratchpad. No adb, APK, deploy, npm install or git write commands.

issues.problem: The fix is correct, but it cannot meet the item's target (GO!→board ≤ 1.0 s on the joiner) as built. The most it can save is min(X, the push→cover chain), where X is the time from GO! to the game's state, 17–189 ms. When the state comes early (X ≈ 17 ms), the saving is about 17 ms. The GameScreen mount (about 0.5–0.85 s) is still entirely between the state's arrival and the board. APK 19 on P3 was 1.00/1.08 s with sound off, about 1.3 s with sound on and 1.30 s with Reduced Motion, so the sound-on and Reduced Motion runs will almost certainly stay above 1.0 s. The item stays partial for a fourth round.
issues.evidence: From the code: app/friends/room.tsx L152-165 now pushes /game when `go` is non-null. GoCover.tsx L92 only moves from 'cover' to 'under' when !waiting, and gameOnItsWay (L76-78) holds while !info.hasGame. So children (OnlineGame→GameScreen) still mount only after hasGame, exactly as before. Only the work before the mount moved. On a single JS thread, a snapshot that arrives during the push or cover commit is processed after it, so the saving is capped at X. The fixer's own notes (1) say the same. fixcheck-apk19.json go-hold-joiner: P3 off 1.08/1.00, on ~1.3, rm2 1.30 s.
issues.suggestion: Accept this change; it is a safe gain. To reach ≤ 1.0 s, the mount itself has to leave the critical path. One compatible way: the client sends a capability flag in its join options (for example earlySnapshot). For rooms where every client has the flag, GameRoom.countDown launches the game (snapshot with status 'waiting', engine start still at goAt) about 600–800 ms before goAt. Old apps never send the flag, so they keep today's behaviour. On the client, GoCover keeps the cover until GO! has been seen (goFadeFrom already enforces this). Do NOT mount during 3·2·1 on the JS thread without this: the count's step changes come from useNow ticks on JS, and a 0.6 s mount would delay '2'→'1'.

issues.problem: The deviceCheck cannot tell this change apart from noise, and the logcat markers it relies on did not exist in the last release build. The expected effect (0–0.19 s, often near 0) is the same size as the run-to-run spread on P3 in APK 19 (1.00–1.30 s), and the measurement uses 20 ms frame steps. Criterion (a) 'never above the APK 19 numbers' can then pass or fail by chance.
issues.evidence: fixcheck-apk19.json: "No '[friends] GO! shown' line in logcat on either phone (0 hits). I also saw no StatusBarModule line in this build." The deviceCheck still asks for GO!→StatusBarModule from logcat.
issues.suggestion: Add release-visible timestamps (for example a native Log or a console.warn kept in release) at: GO! shown, the /game push, the GoCover cover drawn, the snapshot's arrival (hasGame), the GameScreen mount start, and the first board frame. Then the deviceCheck can measure X and the chain that moved directly, on both phones, over at least 3 runs per condition, and report the median.

issues.problem: While `waiting`, the game screen has nothing that TalkBack can reach. The cover is accessibilityElementsHidden / no-hide-descendants and the children are null, and back is blocked. Usually this lasts 17–189 ms. If the connection drops in that gap (status 'reconnecting' keeps gameOnItsWay true), GO! with 'מכינים את הלוח…' stays up until the reconnect succeeds or gives up, with no reconnect feedback, no way out, and an empty accessibility tree. Before, a drop showed the room's lobby with its reconnecting state (roomPhase.ts case 'reconnecting').
issues.evidence: GoCover.tsx L76-78: gameOnItsWay is true for status 'lobby' and 'reconnecting'. L148 renders children null in 'cover'. L152-157 hides the cover from accessibility. roomPhase.ts L87-97 maps 'reconnecting' to the lobby with reconnecting:true.
issues.suggestion: Make gameOnItsWay false for 'reconnecting', or after a short timeout (for example 2 s past GO!), so OnlineGame's ConnectionLayer (reconnect UI with exits) mounts under the cover. Or give the waiting GO! frame an accessibilityLabel / live region while it waits.

rework.notes:
1) Review, medium (≤1.0 s cannot be reached): accepted as a fact, refuted as something to fix this round. The item stays partial. The saving is capped at X (17–189 ms), and the GameScreen mount (about 0.5–0.85 s) is still between the state's arrival and the board. I did not build the suggested early snapshot (a join flag, launching about 0.7 s before goAt, mounting during the count), for these reasons:
(a) It only helps after a server deploy, and this round forbids deploys. A client that depends on it cannot be checked on the phones in this final round.
(b) Mounting during '1' blocks the JS thread for 0.5–0.85 s, and that same thread drives the count's step change (room.tsx useNow tick) and the GO cue. GO! itself would then come late, which breaks the requirement "without hurting the count's smoothness". Hiding that would mean moving the count's digits to the UI thread, or pushing /game during the count with GoCover drawing 3·2·1. Both rewrite the loop 15 slam and handoff, which the task forbids.
(c) The protocol already sends a 'waiting' snapshot before game.start() (GameRoom.launch L929-934). Splitting launch and start in time also touches seat-away handling, rated config creation (async createConfig) and the stealth bots. It also hands the puzzle to the client up to 0.7 s before GO. That is a design decision for Moshe, not a last-round fix.
The remaining lever that needs no protocol change is to make GameScreen's first commit cheaper (for example, deferring the opponent avatar SVGs or the HUD until after the fade starts). Without a release profile of the mount I cannot say which part is heavy, so I did not guess.
2) Review, low (markers): not added. Mobile logs are __DEV__-only by convention (friendsDevice.ts L72, device.ts L44). Loop 13 deliberately removed the temporary release logcat line so it would not ship, and this build is headed for the store. That removal is why APK 19 had 0 '[friends] GO! shown' hits. Instead, the deviceCheck no longer asks for StatusBarModule or logcat. It asks for ≥3 runs per condition with medians, and states that the expected gain is X-bound and small, so single-run noise is not a fail.
3) Review, low (accessibility and reconnecting): fixed (see fix 4). In the previous version, a drop between GO! and the game's arrival left GO! up, hidden from screen readers, with back blocked, until the reconnect ended. Now ConnectionLayer's reconnecting state (attempts, exits) mounts under GO! and GO! fades into it. While GO! waits alone for the game, screen readers can reach it.
4) A behaviour change remains in a rare case. If the room closes in the 17–189 ms gap, the game route's connection error with its exits is shown instead of the room's 'closed' state, because the room is already out of the history.
5) All 7 changed files are LF (0 CR bytes). prettier was run only on the files I changed. motion.md was rebuilt as HEAD plus my 1-line edit (verified last round). No adb, APK, deploy, npm install or git write commands.

final.notes:
1) Review, medium (≤1.0 s cannot be reached): accepted as a fact, refuted as something to fix this round. The item stays partial. The saving is capped at X (17–189 ms), and the GameScreen mount (about 0.5–0.85 s) is still between the state's arrival and the board. I did not build the suggested early snapshot (a join flag, launching about 0.7 s before goAt, mounting during the count), for these reasons:
(a) It only helps after a server deploy, and this round forbids deploys. A client that depends on it cannot be checked on the phones in this final round.
(b) Mounting during '1' blocks the JS thread for 0.5–0.85 s, and that same thread drives the count's step change (room.tsx useNow tick) and the GO cue. GO! itself would then come late, which breaks the requirement "without hurting the count's smoothness". Hiding that would mean moving the count's digits to the UI thread, or pushing /game during the count with GoCover drawing 3·2·1. Both rewrite the loop 15 slam and handoff, which the task forbids.
(c) The protocol already sends a 'waiting' snapshot before game.start() (GameRoom.launch L929-934). Splitting launch and start in time also touches seat-away handling, rated config creation (async createConfig) and the stealth bots. It also hands the puzzle to the client up to 0.7 s before GO. That is a design decision for Moshe, not a last-round fix.
The remaining lever that needs no protocol change is to make GameScreen's first commit cheaper (for example, deferring the opponent avatar SVGs or the HUD until after the fade starts). Without a release profile of the mount I cannot say which part is heavy, so I did not guess.
2) Review, low (markers): not added. Mobile logs are __DEV__-only by convention (friendsDevice.ts L72, device.ts L44). Loop 13 deliberately removed the temporary release logcat line so it would not ship, and this build is headed for the store. That removal is why APK 19 had 0 '[friends] GO! shown' hits. Instead, the deviceCheck no longer asks for StatusBarModule or logcat. It asks for ≥3 runs per condition with medians, and states that the expected gain is X-bound and small, so single-run noise is not a fail.
3) Review, low (accessibility and reconnecting): fixed (see fix 4). In the previous version, a drop between GO! and the game's arrival left GO! up, hidden from screen readers, with back blocked, until the reconnect ended. Now ConnectionLayer's reconnecting state (attempts, exits) mounts under GO! and GO! fades into it. While GO! waits alone for the game, screen readers can reach it.
4) A behaviour change remains in a rare case. If the room closes in the 17–189 ms gap, the game route's connection error with its exits is shown instead of the room's 'closed' state, because the room is already out of the history.
5) All 7 changed files are LF (0 CR bytes). prettier was run only on the files I changed. motion.md was rebuilt as HEAD plus my 1-line edit (verified last round). No adb, APK, deploy, npm install or git write commands.

items.rootCause: The flake was in the test, not in the app. The first test used the real clock. ResultsLoading (ResultsScreen.tsx:241) turns 'results-loading-shown' to opacity 1 through its own setTimeout after RESULTS_QUIET_MS (300 ms). That is intended: a slow load shows the spinner. Under the load of 'npm run verify', more than 300 ms of wall time passed between render and the check after the first frame. The timer fired during settle() and the check at line 76 saw opacity 1, even though no frame was skipped. It is not a race in the app. On the phone, if the two frames themselves take more than 300 ms, showing the spinner is the behaviour the spec wants. The app does not draw the loading view in the first frame because of the frames. Only the quiet timer's wall time runs out.
items.fix: Test only: apps/mobile/src/screens/results/__tests__/resultsFrames.test.tsx. The first test now runs under jest.useFakeTimers({ doNotFake: ['setImmediate','nextTick','queueMicrotask','requestAnimationFrame','cancelAnimationFrame'] }). The clock stands still, so only the explicit frame() steps (the spied requestAnimationFrame) move the results on, and settle() and the promises still run. A try/finally calls clearAllTimers and useRealTimers. All the original assertions are kept: loading is mounted and invisible after render and after frame 1, and results are drawn after frame 2. No app code changed.

items.rootCause: A loop-15 regression. The room's GO! is a useSlamSince slam timed by the clock from `origin` = goShownAt, which app/friends/room.tsx takes with systemClock.now() while it renders GO! on the JS thread. The slam's first frame on the UI thread comes 45-200 ms later: the render, the commit and the mount, then GoStep's passive effect, then the runOnUI start. Until that frame the view is drawn at opacity 0, which explains the 2-4 empty frames after the '1'. When the clock animation starts, its onStart already reads Date.now()-origin = 45-200 ms. Computed from the slam spring (stiffness 220, damping 15, from 1.4), that is scale ~1.30 at 50 ms, ~1.11 at 116 ms and ~0.95-0.98 at 150-200 ms. These are the QA numbers: first GO! at 1.28-1.32, or at 0.96-0.98 and then landing via 0.94. Before loop 15, useSlam started its spring on its own first frame, so it showed 1.41.
items.fix:
The slam's clock now starts on the owner's first UI frame, not at the JS render time. The game screen's cover still follows the same picture.
- apps/mobile/src/screens/game/connection/motion.ts: a module-level makeMutable `slamDrawnAt` {origin, at}. useSlamSince takes a new `owner` flag. In the clock animation's onStart (UI thread), the owner records Date.now() for its origin once. Every slam with that origin, owner or not, computes its time in each frame as Date.now() - (slamDrawnAt.at if the origins match, otherwise origin). A slam whose owner never ran keeps the old behaviour.
- apps/mobile/src/screens/friends/FriendsCountdown.tsx: GoStep passes owner={!cover}. The room's GO! is the owner. The cover's GO! (FriendsGoFrame, cover) is a reader, so the two stay one picture in the cut, as loop 15 required.
- Reduced motion: unchanged. It still has no scale and only the fade, now starting from the first frame.
- No strings changed.

issues.problem: go-slam-start-skipped: the slam's clock now starts from the owner's first frame (slamDrawnAt.at), but the reader's seed in useSlamSince still uses `origin`. With Reduce Motion on, end = 200 ms. If the cover's GoStep (FriendsGoFrame on the game route) first renders between origin+200 and drawnAt+200, a window 45-200 ms wide, its seed is `end`. withClockSince's animation then has current === end, and Reanimated skips it, as the comment in motion.ts says. So the cover's GO! is fully opaque from its first frame, while the room's GO! under it, timed from drawnAt, is still fading in at about 0.4-0.9 opacity. The result is an opacity jump at the cut, only with Reduce Motion. Before this change, the seed and the clock both used origin, so they agreed. Without Reduce Motion the same window is past 900 ms and invisible (the spring has landed).
issues.evidence: motion.ts:190: `const [seed] = useState(() => (systemClock.now() - origin >= end ? end : 0));`. since() uses `drawn.origin === origin ? drawn.at : origin`. The animation has `current: end` ("Reanimated skips an animation whose target is the value now"). reducedFade is 200 (docs/design/tokens.json:1020). The new test mounts the cover only about 64 ms after a goShownAt of now-100 (164 ms < 200), so this window is never tested.
issues.suggestion: Seed the reader from the same start as its clock. For example, in the seed initializer read slamDrawnAt on JS (makeMutable.get() is a synchronous read of the UI value) and use `drawn.origin === origin ? drawn.at : origin`. Alternatively, seed `end` only once `now - origin >= end + max lag` (for example 250 ms). Add a reduce='on' test case where the cover mounts at about origin+220 with drawnAt about origin+100. It should expect the cover's opacity to equal the room's, not 1.

issues.problem: warp-standby-stalls only helps when the lobby lasts long enough. The lobby now runs 16 earlier steps plus 8 hit players, one per idle moment, so it needs several seconds. If the host taps 'התחל' soon after P3 joins, the in-game fallback (HIT_WARM_DELAY_MS = 1500 after the game mounts) still builds the leftover players at board+1.0-1.3 s, which is exactly where the stalls were measured. items.rootCause:
The 'sound ON only' part comes from the interference sounds' warm-up, made in the board's first seconds.
- useWarmHitCues (screens/game/hit/warmHitCues.ts) starts HIT_WARM_DELAY_MS (1500 ms) after the game screen mounts, under GO!. That is about +1.0-1.3 s after the board's first frame.
- It makes up to 8 expo-audio players: 6 hit kinds, plus arsenalOpen and launch. One player per idle moment, so back to back for about 1 s.
- Each step builds the player on the main thread (runBlocking while JS waits). It then plays it once muted (the Android first-play warm-up in sfx.ts), and that starts ExoPlayer's doSomeWork and an AudioTrack.
- This matches the trace: the 132 ms main-thread gap at +1.74 s during a 91 ms doSomeWork, the 92/136 ms stalls at +1.3 s, and only 6-11 frames per 250 ms from +1.25 to +2.25 s with sound ON. With sound OFF nothing is warmed (sfx.preload returns at once), and only one 53 ms gap was seen.
- The NativeAlloc and concurrent GC that follows, under lmkd criticalLowMemory, is partly the device's memory pressure and partly these allocations.

The +2.25..+3.0 s mounts (4/12/16 views, then 110 views with a 58 ms doFrame) are loop 15's standby banner and the opponent's avatar SVG. They are as designed: the hit's cost moved there on purpose, one avatar per commit. I left them unchanged.
